notes: Formula (113) defines S_A Pi M_G as Pi M-star indexed by G and G prime. The upper-left note specifies that A denotes all edges of G, using the short form ttes. The prose calls this an extension by the lattice Z indexed by A(G). The cancelled upper-right expression and its live equality/bracket marks are retained rather than silently replacing the body’s Pi M indexed by G,G prime.

The page states that Gamma = Aut G acts on the objects and commutes with the canonical morphism (114). It then takes Gamma prime contained in Gamma_G and gives an extension (115), describes its kernel as the local system Z^{A(G)} twisted by Gamma prime’s action, and states a hom to Z^C when C is stable. The variation between Gamma = Aut G and the later notation Gamma_G is preserved as written; no missing definition is supplied from another page.

No proof of the groupoid extension assertions has been checked from this sheet alone. The named objects depend on preceding material not consulted for this assignment. No check-event is claimed merely from reading the formulas. The stable-subset context makes a coordinate projection a plausible interpretation of (116), but the arrow is unlabelled in the ink and no explicit coordinate formula is inserted.

The author’s margin instruction is exactly “expliciter un peu…” and is associated by a long bracket with the subgroup/extension construction. It signals a request for further explanation, not a completed proof on this page. No other authorial question mark is securely identified; the unsure signs in the draft are editorial reading uncertainties.

The comma preceding the cancelled Gamma_G in (114) is untouched and remains in the text, despite the awkward punctuation left by cancelling the following term. The replacement Gamma prime in (115) is written to the left/above the old struck term. The cancelled little de in the first paragraph is visibly interlinear and is represented as an insertion subsequently cancelled.

The noyau sentence is a replacement written above “Soit C un ensemble d”. It is marked inserted; the old wording ends at d and is not completed to de. Its quotation marks are pairs of high strokes, transcribed as two backticks and two apostrophes rather than guillemets.

All four integer Z occurrences have doubled diagonal shafts. They are transcribed with mathbb Z after checking each local occurrence, rather than carrying over C’s bold Z. The lower-row connector in (115) is much shorter and less definite than the upper arrow; its dash/right-arrow doubt is local and does not alter the other arrows.

The pale 84 at the lower left is a source foliation whose hand is not securely attributable. It remains margin{84}. The sheet contains no date. Formula labels (113), (114), (115) and (116) are handwritten at the left and are included in blind boxes.

All fourteen crops were made once from the original, with LANCZOS enlargement, autocontrast, and mild sharpening, and every crop was viewed. The left-note crop was rotated −30 degrees and the expliciter-note crop −40 degrees; all other rotations are zero. Coordinates in every report entry refer to the unrotated original image. No OCR, recognition software, external research, other-page packet, or TeX compilation was used.

Main reader directly inspected the original and all fourteen crops, accepted the local readings and retained doubts, and split the cancelled interlinear insertion into its insertion/deletion inventory entries. H's unreadable subgroup deletion is collated with its displaced position rather than treated as a second physical cancellation.
